match.reason: No bank point teaches how entrepreneurs contribute to society; the closest, Entrepreneurs and change, covers responding to changing conditions and only mentions jobs in passing, and the First Nations point covers a specific business rather than the wider contribution.

draft.title: Entrepreneurs' contribution to society
card: An entrepreneur starts a new business or builds a new idea into a business. Their work can help society in several ways.
Jobs
A new business often hires staff. Those workers earn incomes and spend them in the community, which can help other businesses too.
Products and ways of working
Entrepreneurs can bring new goods and services to customers. They can also find new ways of working, such as a faster delivery method or a new way to sell online.
Community and culture

Some Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander entrepreneurs build businesses on their culture and community, such as sharing bush foods or running cultural tours. These businesses can create jobs and keep culture strong, and the community often shares in the benefits.
draft.remember: Entrepreneurs can create jobs, new products and new ways of working, and some build businesses on culture and community.

a.q: Ava starts a bakery in Orange and hires four local people. Which contribution to society does this show most directly?
opts: Creating jobs in the community
Inventing a new way of working
Building a business on culture
Providing a new type of product
a.why: Hiring four local people creates jobs, and those workers earn incomes they can spend locally. The scenario does not mention a new product or a new method, so a new way of working is the tempting but wrong option.
a.clue: Look at what Ava does for local people.

b.q: Tom runs tours on his Country in New South Wales, where he shares stories and food from his community. He employs two young people from the community. Which statement best describes his contribution to society?
opts: He creates jobs and builds a business on culture
He creates jobs but offers nothing based on culture
He builds on culture but creates no jobs for others
He brings in a new way of working only
b.why: Tom employs two young people, which creates jobs, and his tours are built on culture and community. Both parts of the answer fit the scenario. The option about a new way of working only ignores both of these.
b.clue: Check the scenario for both jobs and culture.

b.best: He creates jobs and builds a business on culture

problems.detail: The clue 'Check the scenario for both jobs and culture' points straight to the only option that names both jobs and culture, so a student could pick it without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The card and both answers are accurate. Question b's clue gives the answer away by telling students to look for both jobs and culture, which only the right option mentions.
